On 2023/05/22 the user asked about how redistricting affects the distribution of political power and its impact on voter turnout and participation. #redistricting #politics

Redistricting discussion point: safe districts (one party reliably wins, often via gerrymandering) vs competitive districts; safe-district voters may feel their vote doesn't matter and abstain, while competitive-district voters are more motivated. #redistricting #voter-turnout

Ways to make redistricting fair: independent nonpartisan commissions, transparent process with public input, objective criteria (equal population, Voting Rights Act compliance) rather than partisan voting history, and judicial review. #redistricting #fair-elections

State redistricting reform examples discussed: California (2010 ballot measure, 14-member independent commission), Arizona (2000 initiative, 5-member commission), Iowa (long-standing nonpartisan legislative services agency process with legislature vote), Colorado (2018 initiative, 12 members chosen by retired judges). #redistricting #independent-commissions

Barriers to redistricting reform: the party in power controls the process and resists giving up power, partisan history/status quo resistance, and commissions may require changes to state law or constitution; progress comes via ballot initiatives and advocacy. #redistricting #reform-barriers

Redistricting reform example: California voters approved an independent redistricting commission in 2010; it has 14 members chosen through a public application process and must be impartial. #redistricting #independent-commissions

Redistricting reform examples: Arizona (2000 ballot initiative, 5-member independent commission) and Colorado (2018 initiative, 12 members chosen by retired judges, must be impartial). #redistricting #independent-commissions

Redistricting reform example: Iowa has used a nonpartisan process for decades, with a nonpartisan legislative services agency drawing proposals from population data and objective criteria, then the legislature votes. #redistricting #independent-commissions

#FreshEarth is a whitepaper project the user is authoring: a regenerative agri-food ecosystem. User will supply source material first and will explicitly say when to start developing/drafting documents — do not draft until told.

#FET (Fresh Earth Token): ERC-20 utility token representing fractional ownership of the Fresh Earth ecosystem; value derived from ecosystem assets plus the future impact of regenerative projects. Governed via a DAO that manages the food ecosystem business.

#FreshEarth ecosystem components: B2B marketplace (regenerative farmers to businesses), B2C marketplace, Project Management Platform, Data Management Platform (measures/validates regenerative impact), and a Rewards System.

#FreshEarth core thesis: industrial agri-food externalizes environmental and health costs, so regenerative farmers are outcompeted. Solution = internalization of costs / accounting for natural capital so regenerative and degenerative methods compete on equal footing, and regeneration itself becomes a revenue stream.

#FreshEarth critique of the monetary system: fractional-reserve, debt-based money creation ("promises to repay") forces commerce to repay debt by liquidating natural capital, since natural capital is unaccounted for; cites IMF loans forcing indebted nations to mine natural capital.

#FreshEarth cost figures cited: externalized damages of the $1T US food industry = $2.1T (2021 Rockefeller report); diet-related chronic disease healthcare = $2T/yr (WHO); deforestation lost ecosystem services $2-5T/yr; biodiversity loss ~$500B/yr; water pollution ~$452B/yr; aggregates to $11-17T in a $100T global GDP. Also: ~33% of food production lost/wasted, ~800M hungry.

#FreshEarth elevator pitch: targets the $13.4 trillion (2023) agri-food market with a global community-based food system; FET creates a positive feedback loop where ecosystem success drives investment, impact, and token value.

#FreshEarth open items still to be resolved: token supply/distribution and limits by country, governance mechanics, technical requirements, team bios, industry and community partnerships, roadmap milestones and dates, legal, token security & auditing, wallet and exchange listing, and references list.

#FreshEarth whitepaper outline, front + framing: Elevator Pitch, Executive Summary; 1 Introduction (purpose/goals of token, classification, summary of what follows); 2 Background (context agrifood-health-environment, externalization of costs, the monetary system, economic costs of the degenerative system).

Protective on-board equipment on the International Space Station (#ISS) is built from materials such as polycarbonate and acrylic plastics (windows/viewing ports), aluminum alloys (structures), stainless steel (high-stress areas), and ceramics (thermal protection shields).
Micrometeoroid and debris protection for the #ISS uses high-strength fibers such as Kevlar, plus radiation shielding materials like polyethylene and lead.

Bubble wrap and duct tape are not used in the construction or repair of #ISS equipment; space-rated materials and specialized tools are used instead, since ordinary items may not meet safety and performance requirements.

#ISS spare parts are kept on Earth in NASA inventory and delivered by cargo vehicles such as SpaceX Dragon and Northrop Grumman Cygnus; failed components beyond repair are replaced, though crews often troubleshoot and repair in orbit.

#ISS crew life: no traditional TV or internet, but movies, music, books, video games, exercise gear, personal items, email/video calls and social media are available. Diet is largely freeze-dried/dehydrated/irradiated food with occasional fresh produce. No pets aboard.
